BURSEVI:v1p318#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p318#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p318#2/r1.claim: The preceding Persian verses portray the spiritually realized as hidden and nameless, united in both outward religious law and inward truth.
BURSEVI:v1p318#2/r1.anchor: تنشان بشريعت هم دلشان بحقيقت هم هم دل شده وهم جان نه اين ونه آن مانده

BURSEVI:v1p318#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p318#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p318#2/r2.claim: The commentator prays for God’s peace and mercy and asks to be counted among those spiritually realized.
BURSEVI:v1p318#2/r2.anchor: عليهم سلام الله ورحمته وبركاته اللهم اجعلنا من اللاحقين بهم

BURSEVI:v1p318#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p318#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p318#2/r3.claim: Saul and his believers emerge into the open battlefield, see the enemy’s forces and equipment, and collectively pray after the fearful group’s hearts have been strengthened by the brave.
BURSEVI:v1p318#2/r3.anchor: ظهر طالوت ومن معه من المؤمنين وصاروا إلى براز

BURSEVI:v1p318#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p318#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p318#2/r4.claim: Calling God ‘our Lord’ acknowledges servitude and seeks their reform, since the word Lord conveys that relation.
BURSEVI:v1p318#2/r4.anchor: في ندائهم بقولهم {ربنا} اعتراف منهم بالعبودية وطلب لإصلاحهم

BURSEVI:v1p318#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p318#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p318#2/r5.claim: ‘Pour upon us’ pictures abundance and completion of patience covering them like a vessel; they ask endurance for battle’s hardships.
BURSEVI:v1p318#2/r5.anchor: إفراغ الإناء إخلاؤه مما فيه أي : صب علينا

BURSEVI:v1p318#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p318#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p318#2/r6.claim: Firm feet signify inner strength, resolve, and steadiness when confronting the enemy, not merely remaining in one physical place.
BURSEVI:v1p318#2/r6.anchor: فالمراد بثبات القدم كمال القوة والرسوخ عند المقارنة وعدم التزلزل وقت المقامة

BURSEVI:v1p318#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p318#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p318#2/r7.claim: Their prayer follows a deliberate order: abundant patience first, firmness arising from it second, and victory over the enemy as the ultimate aim.
BURSEVI:v1p318#2/r7.anchor: حيث قدموا سؤال إفراغ الصبر على قلوبهم الذي هو ملاك الأمر ثم سؤال تثبيت القدم

QUSHAYRI:v1p115/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p115/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p115/r4.claim: They sought victory over the unbelievers as God’s enemies, not revenge for their own loss; acting for God and by God brought victory.
QUSHAYRI:v1p115/r4.anchor: يطلبون النصرة عليهم - لا للانتقام منهم لأجل ما فاتهم من نصيبهم - ولكن

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p93/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p93/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p93/r1.claim: أفرغ علينا صبرا means pour patience over us as one pours from a bucket.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p93/r1.anchor: أي صبه علينا، كما يفرغ الدلو

MAJAZ:v1p77/r10.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p77/r10.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p77/r10.claim: أفرغ علينا صبرا means send patience down upon us.

IBNABIHATIM:v2p477#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p477#2/r1.speaker: وهب بن منبه
IBNABIHATIM:v2p477#2/r1.claim: Wahb recounts David’s duel with Goliath: David refused Saul’s armor, fought with a sling and stones, struck Goliath between the eyes, routed his army, and beheaded him after their wager promised Saul’s daughter and rule over his wealth.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p477#2/r1.anchor: فاخذ داود حجرا ، فرماه بالمقلاع ، فاصاب بين عينيه ، حتى نفذت في دماغه ، فصرخ جالوت وانهزم من معه ، واحتز داود راسه

IBNABIHATIM:v2p477#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p477#2/r2.speaker: الربيع
IBNABIHATIM:v2p477#2/r2.claim: Rabiʿ describes Goliath’s army as numerous and cites the fighters’ prayer for patience, firm footing, and victory.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p477#2/r2.anchor: عن الربيع ، قال : فجاء جالوت في عدد كثير وعدة ولما برزوا لجالوت وجنوده قالوا ربنا افرغ علينا صبرا

IBNABIHATIM:v2p477#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p477#2/r3.speaker: علي بن الحسين
IBNABIHATIM:v2p477#2/r3.claim: At the Resurrection, patient people will be summoned to enter Paradise before the reckoning; they endured obedience and avoided sin until death.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p477#2/r3.anchor: عن علي بن الحسين قال : اذا جمع الله الاولين والاخرين ، ينادي مناد : اين الصابرون ؟ ليدخلوا الجنة قبل الحساب .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p478/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p478/r1.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v2p478/r1.claim: The fighters asked God to make their feet firm.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p478/r1.anchor: قال محمد بن اسحاق : وثبت اقدامنا قال : سالوه ان يثبت اقدامهم

IBNABIHATIM:v2p478/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p478/r2.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v2p478/r2.claim: They sought God’s aid against the unbelieving people.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p478/r2.anchor: قال محمد بن اسحاق وانصرنا على القوم الكفرين قال : استنصروه على القوم الكافرين

IBNABIHATIM:v2p478/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p478/r3.speaker: السدى
IBNABIHATIM:v2p478/r3.claim: Al-Suddi recounts David’s signs and rise: the youngest son’s sling feats, beasts and mountains’ submission, divinely fitting armor, stones that merged, and his killing Goliath before David entered the royal family.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p478/r3.anchor: عن السدى ولما برزوا لجالوت وجنوده قالوا ربنا افرغ علينا صبرا فعبر معه يؤمنذ أبو داود فيمن عبر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p499/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p499/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p499/r4.claim: At the encounter with Goliath, the believers ask God to pour out abundant, encompassing patience; pouring is a metaphor for strength and plenty, illustrated by Abu Kabir al-Hudhali.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p499/r4.anchor: وعبروا عن إلهامهم إلى الصبر بالإفراغ استعارة لقوة الصبر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p499/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p499/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p499/r5.claim: Asking for firm feet is a metaphor for not fleeing: fear and flight resemble a slipping foot, while steadiness in danger resembles planted feet.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p499/r5.anchor: وتثبيت الأقدام استعارة لعدم الفرار شبه الفرار والخوف بزلق القدم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p336#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p336#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p336#2/r1.claim: Barazū means they emerged onto open, spacious ground; Jālūt is a non-Arabic name adapted into Arabic, and ifrāgh is a full and ample pouring-out of patience.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p336#2/r1.anchor: صاروا في البراز وهو الأفيح من الأرض المتسع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p336#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p336#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p336#2/r2.claim: The image of making feet firm evokes stability; the root of defeat means striking something so its parts fold into one another, then came to mean an army's defeat and retreat.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p336#2/r2.anchor: والهزم أصله أن يضرب الشيء فيدخل بعضه في بعض

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p336#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p336#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p336#2/r3.claim: Jālūt was king and commander of the ʿAmālīq; a report numbers his force at three hundred thousand horsemen.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p336#2/r3.anchor: وكان فيما روي في ثلاثمائة ألف فارس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p299/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p299/r1.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p299/r1.claim: Al-Hasan explains “by God’s permission” as by God’s help.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p299/r1.anchor: ﴿ بإذن الله ﴾ قال الحسن بنصر الله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p299/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p299/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p299/r2.claim: God’s being with the steadfast means that He grants them victory and assistance.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p299/r2.anchor: ﴿ والله مع الصابرين ﴾ أي بالنصر والاعانة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p669/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p669/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p669/r1.claim: A small believing force faced Goliath's larger army and asked God to pour patience upon them, steady them against fleeing or failing, and grant victory over the unbelievers.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p669/r1.anchor: لما واجه حزب الإيمان -وهم قليل-من أصحاب طالوت لعدوهم أصحاب جالوت -وهم عدد كثير-

SAMIN-DURR:2:250/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:250/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:250/r1.claim: The ل in لجالوت may attach to برزوا or form a circumstantial phrase with an omitted sense: they advanced intending to meet Goliath.
SAMIN-DURR:2:250/r1.anchor: في هذه اللام وجهان، أحدهما: أنها تتعلق ببرزوا

SAMIN-DURR:2:250/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:250/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:250/r2.claim: برزوا means reaching open, level ground; مبارزة in battle is so called because each opponent is exposed to the other.
SAMIN-DURR:2:250/r2.anchor: ومعنى برزوا صاروا إلى براز من الأرض

SAMIN-DURR:2:250/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:250/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:250/r3.claim: Calling God ربنا acknowledges servitude and asks for their reform, since الرب conveys that relationship.
SAMIN-DURR:2:250/r3.anchor: وفي ندائهم بقولهم: " ربنا " اعتراف منهم بالعبودية وطلب لإصلاحهم

SAMIN-DURR:2:250/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:250/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:250/r4.claim: على in أفرغ علينا asks that patience be over and encompass them, like a vessel surrounding its contents.
SAMIN-DURR:2:250/r4.anchor: وأتوا بلفظ " على " في قولهم: " أفرغ علينا " طلبا لأن يكون الصبر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p323#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p323#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p323#2/r1.claim: Goliath was a giant Amalekite descended from ʿAmliq son of ʿĀd; his helmet weighed three hundred ratls.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p323#2/r1.anchor: جبار من العمالقة من اولاد عمليق بن عاد وكانت بيضته فيها ثلثمائة رطل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p323#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p323#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p323#2/r2.claim: Asking God to steady their feet means granting battlefield resilience through courage, striking fear into the enemy, and similar means.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p323#2/r2.anchor: وهب لنا ما نثبت به في مداحض الحرب من قوة القلوب والقاء الرعب في قلب العدو

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p323#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p323#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p323#2/r3.claim: David, Jesse’s youngest son and a shepherd, was the seventh son in Talut’s army; revelation told Samuel he would kill Goliath, and David slew him with three stones that called to him.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p323#2/r3.anchor: كان ايشى أبو داود في عسكر طالوت مع ستة من بنيه وكان داود سابعهم وهو صغير يرعى الغنم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p323#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p323#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p323#2/r4.claim: Talut married his daughter to David after David killed Goliath.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p323#2/r4.anchor: ورمى بها جالوت فقتله وزوجه طالوت بنته

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p323#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p323#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p323#2/r5.claim: Another report says Talut envied David and sought to kill him, then repented.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p323#2/r5.anchor: وروي انه حسده واراد قتله ثم تاب

MUQATIL:2:250-251/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:250-251/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:250-251/r1.claim: The companions of the chamber asked God to pour patience over them and keep their feet steady in battle; “pour” also describes pouring molten metal in 18:96.
MUQATIL:2:250-251/r1.anchor: يعنى ألق، أصبب علينا صبرا، كقوله سبحانه:

NASAFI-FULL:v1p121#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p121#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p121#2/r1.claim: They went out to fight Goliath and his troops, asking God to pour patience on them in battle and help them against the disbelievers.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p121#2/r1.anchor: خرجوا لقتالهم ﴿ قالوا ربنا أفرغ ﴾ أصبب ﴿ علينا صبرا ﴾ على القتال

NASAFI-FULL:v1p121#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p121#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p121#2/r2.claim: Firm steps mean strengthening their hearts and casting terror into the enemy's hearts.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p121#2/r2.anchor: بتقوية قلوبنا والقاء الرعب فى صدور عدونا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:250/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:250/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:250/r1.claim: برزوا means they came into the open, broad plain land.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:250/r1.anchor: برزوا } صاروا في البراز وهو الأفيح من الأرض المتسع.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:250/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:250/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:250/r2.claim: Jalut was king and commander of the Amalekites, said to cast a one-mile shadow; the Berbers are said to descend from him, and one report numbers his force at 300,000 cavalry.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:250/r2.anchor: وكان جالوت أمير العمالقة وملكهم ظله ميل. ويقال:، إن البربر من نسله،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:250/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:250/r3.speaker: عكرمة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:250/r3.claim: He gives Jalut's force as 90,000 rather than the other report's 300,000.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:250/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:250/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:250/r4.claim: Seeing the enemy's great numbers, the believers supplicated, as in the account of the many prophets' followers who prayed for forgiveness.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:250/r4.anchor: ولما رأى المؤمنون كثرة عدوهم تضرعوا إلى ربهم وهذا كقوله:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:250/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:250/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:250/r5.claim: The Prophet would say in battle that by God he attacks and maneuvers, and would seek protection from the enemy's evil while asking God to meet them at their throats.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:250/r5.anchor: وكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا لقي العدو يقول في القتال: «اللهم بك أصول وأجول»

QURTUBI-FULL:2:250/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:250/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:250/r6.claim: At Badr he prayed until his cloak fell from his shoulders, urgently asking God to fulfill His promise; the account is discussed under Āl ʿImrān.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:250/r6.anchor: ودعا يوم بدر حتى سقط رداؤه عن منكبيه يستنجز الله وعده

RAZI-FULL:v6p157#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p157#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p157#2/r1.claim: Mubāraza is a combat in which each fighter comes out to face the other; barāz names open ground without a barrier, where each can see the opponent.
RAZI-FULL:v6p157#2/r1.anchor: المبارزة في الحروب ، هي أن يبرز كل واحد منهم لصاحبه

RAZI-FULL:v6p157#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p157#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p157#2/r2.claim: Talut’s army prayed when they faced a numerically superior force, having learned that victory depends on God; the author parallels the prayer with believers at Uhud.
RAZI-FULL:v6p157#2/r2.anchor: ورأوا القلة في جانبهم ، والكثرة في جانب عدوهم

RAZI-FULL:v6p157#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p157#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p157#2/r3.claim: The author says the Prophet regularly prayed for divine help in battle, citing reports that he prayed at Badr for God to fulfill His promise and sought protection from an enemy’s harm.
RAZI-FULL:v6p157#2/r3.anchor: وروي عنه في قصة بدر أنه عليه السلام لم يزل يصلي

RAZI-FULL:v6p157#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p157#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p157#2/r4.claim: Ifrāgh literally means pouring out a vessel’s contents; applying it to patience intensifies the request because it suggests a settled, complete outpouring.
RAZI-FULL:v6p157#2/r4.anchor: أفرغت الإناء إذا صببت ما فيه ، وأصله من الفراغ

RAZI-FULL:v6p157#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p157#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p157#2/r5.claim: The image intensifies the prayer in two ways: poured contents are made to remain, and emptying a vessel entails pouring all that it contains.
RAZI-FULL:v6p157#2/r5.anchor: يدل على المبالغة في طلب الصبر من وجهين

RAZI-FULL:v6p158/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p158/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p158/r1.claim: Combat requires courage before frightening events, equipment and circumstances that enable steadfastness, and strength to overcome the enemy; the three requests correspond to these needs.
RAZI-FULL:v6p158/r1.anchor: الأمور المطلوبة عند المحاربة مجموع أمور ثلاثة فأولها : أن يكون الإنسان صبورا

RAZI-FULL:v6p158/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p158/r2.speaker: الأصحاب
RAZI-FULL:v6p158/r2.claim: The Ashʿarite theologians use the prayer for patience and firm feet to argue that both human resolve and the resulting steadfastness are created by God.
RAZI-FULL:v6p158/r2.anchor: احتج الأصحاب على أن أفعال العباد مخلوقة لله تعالى بقوله

RAZI-FULL:v6p158/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p158/r3.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v6p158/r3.claim: Al-Qadi interprets the requests as asking God to create causes of patience and firmness, including fear among enemies, their division, calamities, disease, or a leader’s death.
RAZI-FULL:v6p158/r3.anchor: أجاب القاضي عنه بأن المراد من الصبر وتثبيت القدم تحصيل أسباب الصبر

RAZI-FULL:v6p158/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p158/r4.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v6p158/r4.claim: Among the causes Al-Qadi lists are terror that unsettles the enemy and weakness or illness that occupies or incapacitates them, thereby emboldening believers.
RAZI-FULL:v6p158/r4.anchor: أن يجعل في قلوب أعدائهم الرعب والجبن منهم فيقع بسبب ذلك منهم الاضطراب

RAZI-FULL:v6p158/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p158/r5.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v6p158/r5.claim: Al-Qadi also includes God guiding some enemies to recognize their error, causing disagreement and division that strengthens the believers’ resolve.
RAZI-FULL:v6p158/r5.anchor: أن يلطف ببعض أعدائهم في معرفة بطلان ما هم عليه فيقع بينهم الاختلاف والتفرق

RAZI-FULL:v6p158#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p158#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p158#2/r1.claim: Al-Razi rejects Al-Qadi’s figurative reading: patience is resolve and firmness is stillness, so the verse directly attributes both to God; abandoning the apparent meaning needs evidence.
RAZI-FULL:v6p158#2/r1.anchor: دلت هذه الآية على أن إرادة العبد ومراده من الله تعالى وذلك يبطل قولكم

RAZI-FULL:v6p158#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p158#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p158#2/r2.claim: Even if the requested causes are granted to come from God, either they affect the balance of motives or they do not; on either branch, the Muʿtazilite account cannot avoid divine determination of the outcome.
RAZI-FULL:v6p158#2/r2.anchor: هذه الأسباب التي سلمتم أنها بفعل الله تعالى إذا حصلت ووجدت فهل لها أثر

STUDYQURAN:2:250/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:250/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:250/r1.claim: The account assumes the familiar story in which the young David, chosen by Saul as Israel’s champion, kills Goliath with a sling stone.
STUDYQURAN:2:250/r1.anchor: though a young boy, David is appointed by Saul to face Goliath as the Israelites’ champion

STUDYQURAN:2:250/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:250/r2.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:2:250/r2.claim: David’s wisdom means he inherited Samuel’s prophethood, while his sovereignty means he inherited Saul’s kingship.
STUDYQURAN:2:250/r2.anchor: he inherited the prophethood of Samuel, and sovereignty, meaning he inherited the kingship of Saul

STUDYQURAN:2:250/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:250/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:250/r3.claim: The account of David’s prophethood and reign is further described in 38:17–29.
STUDYQURAN:2:250/r3.anchor: For further description of David and his prophethood and reign, see 38:17–29

TAB-FULL:v4p497#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p497#3/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p497#3/r1.claim: The explanation links tabarraza to going out onto open land to relieve oneself, just as taghawwata is named after going to low ground.
TAB-FULL:v4p497#3/r1.anchor: كما قيل تغوط لأنهم كانوا يقضون حاجتهم في الغائط

TAB-FULL:v4p511/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p511/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p511/r1.claim: The narrative says the armies gathered, David volunteered against Jalut, combined stones named Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and a stone struck Jalut through the head and routed his forces.
TAB-FULL:v4p511/r1.anchor: فكن حجرا واحدا، قال: فأخذهن وأخذ مقلاعا

TAB-FULL:v4p511/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p511/r2.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v4p511/r2.claim: After crossing the river, Talut offered half his kingdom to whoever killed Jalut; David left his flock, volunteered despite his brothers’ scorn, and Talut armed him.
TAB-FULL:v4p511/r2.anchor: فقال طالوت للناس: لو أن جالوت قتل أعطيت الذي يقتله نصف ملكي

TAB-FULL:v4p511/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p511/r3.speaker: ابن جريج عن مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v4p511/r3.claim: Mujahid’s report says David took three stones; they spoke of earlier victories, joined together, promised to aid him, and foretold that the stone would kill Jalut with God’s help.
TAB-FULL:v4p511/r3.anchor: قال ابن جريج: قال مجاهد: كان بعث أبو داود مع داود

TABATABAI:2:249-251/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:249-251/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:249-251/r4.claim: “They appeared before Goliath” uses appearance for emerging to battle; pouring patience is a subtle implied metaphor for God imparting it according to each person’s capacity.
TABATABAI:2:249-251/r4.anchor: البروز هو الظهور، ومنه البراز وهو الظهور للحرب

TABATABAI:2:249-251/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:249-251/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:249-251/r5.claim: Firming the feet is a metonym for steadfastness and not fleeing; “they routed them” means they drove them back.
TABATABAI:2:249-251/r5.anchor: وكذا تثبيت الاقدام كناية عن الثبات وعدم الفرار

ZAJJAJ:v1p332/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p332/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p332/r2.claim: أفرغ علينا صبرا means ‘pour patience over us,’ like pouring the contents from a vessel.
ZAJJAJ:v1p332/r2.anchor:
(ربنا أفرغ علينا صبرا).
أي أصبب علينا الصبر صبا، كما تقول: أفرغت الإناء

TABRISI:2:250/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:250/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:250/r1.claim: Burūz is appearing into open view; afrāgh is pouring liquid so as to empty a vessel, and تثبيت makes something firm in its place.
TABRISI:2:250/r1.anchor: والإفراغ الصب للسيال على جهة إخلاء المكان منه

TABRISI:2:250/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:250/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:250/r2.claim: Victory is aid against an enemy through increased strength, fear, exposure of weakness, imagined numbers, or division; divine victory is always لطف, though not every لطف is victory.
TABRISI:2:250/r2.anchor: والفرق بين النصر واللطف أن كل نصر من الله فهو لطف وليس كل لطف نصرا

TABRISI:2:250/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:250/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:250/r3.claim: Patience is the servant's restraint from an urged action, here restraint from fleeing combat, and it is rewarded.
TABRISI:2:250/r3.anchor: والصبر من فعل العبد لأنه يجازي عليه وهو حبس النفس

TABRISI:2:250/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:250/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:250/r4.claim: When Ṭālūt's believers faced Jālūt, they asked God to grant full patience, likened to pouring all a vessel holds, and to enable steadfastness and victory in jihad.
TABRISI:2:250/r4.anchor: أي وفقنا للصبر على الجهاد وشبهه بتفريغ الإناء

THALABI:v2p217/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p217/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p217/r5.claim: Barazu means Talut and his believing troops came onto open, level ground before Goliath's forces.
THALABI:v2p217/r5.anchor: ولما برزوا يعني طالوت وجنوده المؤمنين لجالوت وجنوده المشركين

THALABI:v2p217/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p217/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p217/r6.claim: Their prayer asks God to pour down patience as one pours from a bucket, strengthen their hearts, and grant victory over the unbelievers.
THALABI:v2p217/r6.anchor: ربنا أفرغ أنزل وأصبب علينا صبرا كما يفرغ الدلو

THALABI:v2p217/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p217/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p217/r7.claim: The verse leaves an implied response: God sent them patience and victory, so they routed the enemy by His leave and David killed Goliath.
THALABI:v2p217/r7.anchor: فأنزل الله عليهم صبرا ونصرا فهزموهم بإذن الله وقتل داود جالوت

THALABI:v2p217#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p217#2/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p217#2/r4.claim: Goliath challenged Talut to send a champion, offering his kingdom if killed; Talut promised his daughter and half the kingdom, but everyone feared Goliath.
THALABI:v2p217#2/r4.anchor: فأرسل جالوت إلى طالوت أن ابرز

THALABI:v2p217#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p217#2/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p217#2/r5.claim: Samuel prayed; God gave a horn of oil and an iron furnace as signs: the chosen warrior's head would receive the horn and fill the furnace, but no Israelite son passed.
THALABI:v2p217#2/r5.anchor: فأتى بقرن فيه دهن، وتنور من حديد، فقيل: إن صاحبكم الذي يقتل جالوت

THALABI:v2p217#2/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p217#2/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p217#2/r6.claim: God revealed that Jesse's son would kill Goliath; his twelve tall sons failed the test, and God told Samuel He judges hearts rather than bodies.
THALABI:v2p217#2/r6.anchor: إنا لا نأخذ الرجال على صورهم ولكنا نأخذ على صلاح قلوبهم

THALABI:v2p217#2/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p217#2/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p217#2/r7.claim: Jesse at first denied having another son, then admitted that small, slight David was hidden among the sheep because he was embarrassed by his short stature.
THALABI:v2p217#2/r7.anchor: إن لي ابنا صغيرا يقال له: داود، استحييت أن يراه الناس لقصر قامته

THALABI:v2p218/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p218/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p218/r1.claim: David carried two sheep at a time across floodwater without wading; Samuel saw his mercy to animals as a sign of mercy to people, anointed him, and the oil overflowed.
THALABI:v2p218/r1.anchor: فوجده يحمل شاتين شاتين يجيزهما السيل ولا يخوض بهما الماء

THALABI:v2p218/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p218/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p218/r2.claim: Talut offered his daughter and a share of the kingdom for Goliath's death; David said he could fight because he had rescued sheep from lions, tigers, and wolves by tearing their jaws.
THALABI:v2p218/r2.anchor: أنا أرعى فيجيء الأسد والنمر والذئب فيأخذ شاة

THALABI:v2p218/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p218/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p218/r3.claim: Talut gave David horse, armor, and weapons, but David returned, saying weapons could not help unless God supported him, and asked to fight his own way.
THALABI:v2p218/r3.anchor: إن الله إن لم ينصرني لا يغني عني السلاح شيئا

THALABI:v2p218/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p218/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p218/r4.claim: On the way David's bag received three speaking stones: Aaron's, Moses's, and the stone God had hidden for David to kill Goliath.
THALABI:v2p218/r4.anchor: فإني حجرك الذي تقتل بي جالوت، وقد خبأني الله لك

THALABI:v2p218/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p218/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p218/r5.claim: Goliath, armed in a helmet with three hundred iron pieces, mocked David's sling; David answered, and Goliath threatened to feed his flesh to animals and birds.
THALABI:v2p218/r5.anchor: وكان له بيضة فيها ثلاث مائة من حديد، فلما نظر إلى داود

THALABI:v2p218/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p218/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p218/r6.claim: David invoked the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob over the three stones; they fused, and a God-driven wind sent the stone through Goliath's helmet and brain, killing thirty behind him and routing the army.
THALABI:v2p218/r6.anchor: فصار كلها حجرا واحدا، ودور المقلاع ورماه به فسخر الله الريح

THALABI:v2p218/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p218/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p218/r7.claim: David killed Goliath and dragged his body before Talut.
THALABI:v2p218/r7.anchor: وهزم الله سبحانه الجيش وخر جالوت قتيلا فأخذه فجره

THALABI:v2p219/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p219/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p219/r1.claim: The victorious army returned safely and wealthy, and people praised David.
THALABI:v2p219/r1.anchor: ففرح المسلمون فرحا شديدا وانصرفوا إلى المدينة سالمين غانمين

THALABI:v2p219/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p219/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p219/r2.claim: Talut demanded two hundred enemy foreskins as a dowry; David killed them, returned the foreskins strung together, married the king's daughter, and received his signet in the kingdom.
THALABI:v2p219/r2.anchor: إذا قتلت منهم مائتي رجل وجئتني بغلفهم زوجتك ابنتي

THALABI:v2p219/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p219/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p219/r3.claim: As David grew popular, Talut became jealous and planned to kill him; Talut's daughter warned David that her father would attack that night.
THALABI:v2p219/r3.anchor: فمال الناس إلى داود وأحبوه وأكثروا ذكره، فوجد طالوت من ذلك

THALABI:v2p219/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p219/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p219/r4.claim: David hid a wine skin in his bed; Talut struck it, saw wine spill, and left assuming David had been drinking.
THALABI:v2p219/r4.anchor:
فوضعه في مضجعه على السرير.
وسجاه ودخل تحت السرير

THALABI:v2p219/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p219/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p219/r5.claim: Afterward Talut sealed and guarded his doors, fearing David would retaliate for the attempted murder.
THALABI:v2p219/r5.anchor: فشدد حجابه وحراسه وأغلق دونه أبوابه

THALABI:v2p219/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p219/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p219/r6.claim: David entered while God blinded the guards, left arrows around Talut, and escaped; Talut recognized that David spared him though he could have killed him.
THALABI:v2p219/r6.anchor: فوضع سهما عند رأسه وسهما عند رجليه وسهما عن يمينه

THALABI:v2p220/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p220/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p220/r1.claim: On a later visit, David again passed blinded guards, took Talut's water jug and cup, cut beard hairs and a piece of his garment, and escaped.
THALABI:v2p220/r1.anchor: وأخذ إبريق طالوت الذي كان يتوضأ منه وكوزه الذي كان يشرب منه

THALABI:v2p220/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p220/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p220/r2.claim: Talut searched for David with spies; later, while riding after him, he lost sight of him when David escaped into a cave.
THALABI:v2p220/r2.anchor: سلط على داود العيون وطلبه أشد الطلب فلم يقدر عليه

THALABI:v2p220/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p220/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p220/r3.claim: God had a spider weave a web over the cave entrance; Talut assumed David had not entered because the web was intact, and David went to worship in the mountains.
THALABI:v2p220/r3.anchor: فأوحى الله تعالى إلى العنكبوت فنسجت عليه بيتا

THALABI:v2p220/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p220/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p220/r4.claim: Talut killed scholars and worshipers who criticized his pursuit of David, and killed every scholar he could find while continuing to win battles.
THALABI:v2p220/r4.anchor: فجعل طالوت لا ينهاه أحد عن قتل داود إلا قتله

THALABI:v2p220/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p220/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p220/r5.claim: Talut ordered a woman who knew God's greatest name to be killed; her executioner spared her in case a scholar would later be needed, prompting Talut's remorse.
THALABI:v2p220/r5.anchor: فأمر جبارا بقتلها فرحمها الجبار فقال: لعلنا نحتاج إلى عالم

THALABI:v2p220/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p220/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p220/r6.claim: Talut wept at the graves asking whether he could repent; the dead rebuked him for disturbing them after killing them, and he wept more.
THALABI:v2p220/r6.anchor: أنشد الله عبدا يعلم أن لي توبة إلا أخبرني بها

THALABI:v2p220/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p220/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p220/r7.claim: The executioner compared him to a king who killed every rooster after one startled him, then wanted roosters to wake him, asking whether he had left one.
THALABI:v2p220/r7.anchor:
إذا صاح الديك فأيقضونا حتى ندلج.
فقالوا: هل تركت ديكا

THALABI:v2p221/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p221/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p221/r1.claim: The executioner completes the parable: Talut had also killed every scholar and could not now find one to advise him.
THALABI:v2p221/r1.anchor: ولكن هل تركت عالما في الأرض

THALABI:v2p221/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p221/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p221/r2.claim: The executioner worried that Talut might kill the sage, but Talut promised not to; he learned the saved woman knew God's greatest name.
THALABI:v2p221/r2.anchor:
أرأيتك إن دللتك على عالم لعلك أن تقتله.
قال: لا

THALABI:v2p221/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p221/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p221/r3.claim: When Talut came, the executioner entered first so the woman would not be frightened, reminding her he had saved and sheltered her before asking about the king's repentance.
THALABI:v2p221/r3.anchor: ألست أعظم الناس عليك منة أن نجيتك من القتل وآويتك عندي

THALABI:v2p221/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p221/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p221/r4.claim: The woman said she knew no repentance for Talut, but asked whether they knew a prophet's grave; she prayed at Samuel's grave and called him out.
THALABI:v2p221/r4.anchor: والله لا أعلم لطالوت توبة، ولكن هل تعلمون مكان قبر نبي

THALABI:v2p221/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p221/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p221/r5.claim: Samuel rose with dust on his head and asked whether the resurrection had begun; they said Talut wanted to know if he could repent.
THALABI:v2p221/r5.anchor: فخرج أشمويل من القبر فنفض من رأسه التراب

THALABI:v2p221/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p221/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p221/r6.claim: Talut admitted he had committed every evil and asked for repentance; Samuel asked how many sons he had, and Talut said ten.
THALABI:v2p221/r6.anchor:
ما فعلت بعدي؟
قال: لم أدع من الشر شيئا إلا فعلته

THALABI:v2p221/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p221/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p221/r7.claim: Samuel said repentance required relinquishing the throne, taking his sons to God's cause, letting them die in battle before him, then fighting and dying himself.
THALABI:v2p221/r7.anchor: أن تتخلى من ملكك وتخرج أنت وولدك في سبيل الله

THALABI:v2p221/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p221/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p221/r8.claim: Samuel returned to the grave and died; Talut went back grief-stricken, fearing his sons would not follow, and wept until his body wasted.
THALABI:v2p221/r8.anchor: ورجع طالوت أحزن ما كان رهبة

THALABI:v2p221/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p221/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p221/r9.claim: Talut asked his sons whether they would ransom him from the Fire; they agreed to do so, and he told them they faced the Fire if they refused his request.
THALABI:v2p221/r9.anchor: أرأيتم لو دفعت إلى النار هل كنتم تفدونني

THALABI:v2p221/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p221/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p221/r10.claim: Talut outfitted himself and his ten sons; they fought and died before him, and then Talut fought and was killed.
THALABI:v2p221/r10.anchor: فتجهز بماله وولده، فقدم ولده وكانوا عشرة فقاتلوا

THALABI:v2p222/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p222/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p222/r1.claim: The man who killed Talut came to David with the news; David said the killer should not live after Talut and beheaded him.
THALABI:v2p222/r1.anchor: فقال: ما كنت بالذي تحيا بعده فضرب عنقه

THALABI:v2p222/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p222/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p222/r2.claim: The Israelites gave David Talut's treasuries and made him king.
THALABI:v2p222/r2.anchor: وأتى بنو إسرائيل بداود فأعطوه خزائن طالوت وملكوه

THALABI:v2p222/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p222/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p222/r3.claim: Talut's reign lasted forty years until he died campaigning with his sons; al-Dahhak and al-Kalbi say David ruled sixty-nine years after Goliath.
THALABI:v2p222/r3.anchor: قال الضحاك والكلبي: ملك داود بعد جالوت تسعا وستين سنة

THALABI:v2p222/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p222/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p222/r4.claim: Israel never united under one king except David, and the commentary gives David's genealogy back through Jacob, Isaac, and Abraham.
THALABI:v2p222/r4.anchor: ولم يجتمع بنو إسرائيل على ملك واحد إلا على داود

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p338#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p338#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p338#2/r1.claim: Ifrāgh literally means pouring and emptying a vessel; the prayer asks God to pour the fullest and most complete patience upon them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p338#2/r1.anchor: فمعنى {ربنا أفرغ علينا صبرا} أي: اصبب (¬5) علينا أتم صب وأبلغه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p338#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p338#2/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p338#2/r2.claim: The request to steady their feet may mean strengthen their hearts, divide the enemy so they falter, cast fear into them so they show weakness, or provide any comparable cause of victory.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p338#2/r2.anchor: {وثبت أقدامنا} بتقوية قلوبنا، أو باختلاف كلمة الأعداء حتى يتخاذلوا،

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:250-252/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:250-252/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:250-252/r1.claim: When they faced Goliath’s army, they prayed for patience to be poured on them and for their feet to be strengthened by strengthening their hearts.

ELMALILI:2:249-252#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:249-252#2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:249-252#2/r5.claim: Facing Goliath's army, the believers collectively ask God to pour patience upon them, keep their feet firm and their resolve steady, and grant victory over the unbelievers.
ELMALILI:2:249-252#2/r5.anchor: ayaklarımızı denk ve yerinde tut, titretme, kaydırma, azm ü hedefimizden şaşırtma

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:249/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:249/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:249/r4.claim: The Philistines were powerful and their commander Goliath was exceptionally large and strong; as the armies neared, fear and demoralization appeared among the Israelites.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:249/r4.anchor: Filistîler güçlü bir düşmandı, başlarında da Câlût (Golyat) isimli çok iri ve güçlü bir savaşçı kumandanları vardı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:249/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:249/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:249/r5.claim: A small group of fighters with strong faith and courage tried to raise morale by recalling that victory belongs to those with the material and spiritual prerequisites, not necessarily the larger army, and by urging hope in God's aid for those fighting in His path.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:249/r5.anchor: zaferin her zaman sayıca üstün olanlara değil, maddî ve mânevî şartlarını haiz olanlara ait olduğunu hatırlattılar

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:249/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:249/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:249/r6.claim: Their prayer for patience and firmness also served as an exhortation to resist and stand steadfast.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:249/r6.anchor: Bu dua aynı zamanda direnme ve sebat gösterme konusunda bir telkin mahiyetinde idi

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p596/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p596/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p596/r5.claim: At face-to-face battle, they seek God's help for endurance, firm footing on slippery ground, and victory over unbelievers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p596/r5.anchor: وحين برزوا لأعدائهم، ووقعت العين على العين لجأوا إلى الله تعالى بالدعاء والاستغاثة،

ALUSI-FULL:v2p172/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p172/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p172/r1.claim: Barazū means Ṭālūt and his company emerged into an open, level stretch of land opposite Goliath and his troops for combat.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p172/r1.anchor: أي ظهر طالوت ومن معه وصاروا في براز من الأرض وهو ما أنكشف منها وأستوى لجالوت وجنوده

ALUSI-FULL:v2p172/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p172/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p172/r2.claim: The whole army prayed after the weak-hearted had gained courage, humbly turning to God and disavowing their own power.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p172/r2.anchor: بعد أن قويت قلوب الضعفاء متضرعين إلى الله تعالى متبرئين

ALUSI-FULL:v2p172/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p172/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p172/r3.claim: Asking God to pour patience means to grant and enable self-restraint in battle; asking to stabilize their feet means complete strength and steadfastness in confrontation, not merely keeping their feet in one spot.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p172/r3.anchor: أي صب ذلك علينا ووفقنا له والمراد به حبس النفس للقتال

ALUSI-FULL:v2p172/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p172/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p172/r4.claim: They ask for aid through the enemy's defeat and rout; calling Goliath's force 'the unbelieving people' instead of using a pronoun states the reason they deserve victory.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p172/r4.anchor: أي أعنا عليهم بقهرهم وهزمهم ووضع

ALUSI-FULL:v2p172/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p172/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p172/r5.claim: The prayer invokes God's nurturing lordship, pictures abundant patience poured like water to cool their hearts and replace withheld water, makes them vessels through ʿalā, and magnifies patience with an indefinite noun.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p172/r5.anchor: فيه التوسل بوصف الربوبية المنبئة عن التبليغ إلى الكمال وأما ثانيا فلأن فيه الإفراغ

ALUSI-FULL:v2p172/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p172/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p172/r6.claim: The sequence is apt: patience at encounter, steadfast strength against the enemy, then victory; patience alone may lack resistance, and courage without victory yields no benefit.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p172/r6.anchor: حيث طلبوا أولا إفراغ الصبر على قلوبهم عند اللقاء وثانيا ثبات القدم والقوة

ALUSI-FULL:v2p172/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p172/r7.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v2p172/r7.claim: An alternative says patience is the foundation, stability follows from it, and victory is the ultimate aim; though this seems to call for fāʾ, the reply says wāw better relies on the mind's natural ordering, as al-Sakkākī notes.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p172/r7.anchor: وقيل : إنما طلبوا أولا إفراغ الصبر لأنه ملاك الأمر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p302/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p302/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p302/r1.claim: The believers led by Talut emerge to face Jalut and his polytheist forces; barazū means coming out onto open, level ground.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p302/r1.anchor: {ولما برزوا} يعني طالوت وجنوده يعني المؤمنين {لجالوت وجنوده} المشركين ومعنى برزوا صاروا بالبراز من الأرض

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p302/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p302/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p302/r2.claim: Afriġ means send or pour down; their request to steady their feet means to steady their hearts.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p302/r2.anchor: {قالوا ربنا أفرغ علينا} أنزل واصبب {صبرا وثبت أقدامنا} قلوبنا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p302/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p302/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p302/r3.claim: They ask God for victory over the unbelieving people.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:249-250#2/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:249-250#2/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:249-250#2/r1.claim: The army turns to God in prayer; the rhetorical sequence first asks for patience as the essential foundation, then steadfast footing in battle, then victory that usually follows.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:249-250#2/r1.anchor: التجؤوا إلى الله سبحانه وتعالى بالدعاء، وفيه ترتيب بليغ إذ سألوا أولا إفراغ الصبر في قلوبهم الذي هو ملاك الأمر

BIQAI-FULL:v1p479/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p479/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p479/r5.claim: The Israelites go out while weak and few against Goliath's troops, who are strong, numerous, bold, and accustomed to victory.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p479/r5.anchor: وهم على ما هم عليه من الضعف والقلة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p479/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p479/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p479/r6.claim: Baraz means leaving whatever conceals one and entering exposed open ground where an observer can see.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p479/r6.anchor: والبروز هو الخروج عن كل شيء يوارى في براز من الأرض

BIQAI-FULL:v1p479/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p479/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p479/r7.claim: Goliath is identified as a king among the Canaanites who lived in Syria in the time of the Israelites.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p479/r7.anchor: اسم ملك من ملوك الكنعانيين كان بالشام في زمن بني إسرائيل

BIQAI-FULL:v1p479/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p479/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p479/r8.claim: Their request to have patience poured over them asks for patience to fill them until they can strike as they wish in battle.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p479/r8.anchor: من الإفراغ وهو السكب المفيض على كلية المسكوب عليه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p479/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p479/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p479/r9.claim: Asking God to steady their feet means strengthening hearts against flight and making their blows forceful.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p479/r9.anchor: أي بتقوية قلوبنا حتى لا نفر وتكون ضرباتنا منكبة موجعة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p479/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p479/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p479/r10.claim: They say against the disbelievers rather than against them to show that they fight for God's neglected rights, not personal advantage, and need God's help against a powerful foe.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p479/r10.anchor: إلى أنهم إنما يقاتلونهم لتضييعهم حقه سبحانه وتعالى لا لحظ من حظوظ النفس

JISHUMI:v2p988#2/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p988#2/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p988#2/r1.claim: Baraza means to appear; here the fighters came out into open terrain.
JISHUMI:v2p988#2/r1.anchor: البروز: أصله الظهور، وبرزوا معناه صاروا بالبراز من الأرض، وهو ما ظهر.

JISHUMI:v2p988#2/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p988#2/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p988#2/r2.claim: Ifrāgh is pouring a liquid so that a space is emptied; its root is emptiness.
JISHUMI:v2p988#2/r2.anchor: والإفراغ: صب السيال على جهة إخلاء المكان منه؛ لأن أصله الخلو،

JISHUMI:v2p988#2/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p988#2/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p988#2/r3.claim: The author cites 28:10, where Moses' mother's heart becomes empty, as an example of the root meaning emptiness.
JISHUMI:v2p988#2/r3.anchor: ومنه: (وأصبح فؤاد أم موسى فارغا) أي خاليا.

JISHUMI:v2p988#2/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p988#2/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p988#2/r4.claim: Thabāt derives from remaining firmly in place; God makes the firm word support believers so they stay on the path of truth.
JISHUMI:v2p988#2/r4.anchor: والثبات: أصله اللزوم، ومنه: القول الثابت الذي يؤيدهم به ليلزموا طريق الحق،

JISHUMI:v2p988#2/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p988#2/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p988#2/r5.claim: Ṣabr is restraining the self from what it is pulled toward.
JISHUMI:v2p988#2/r5.anchor: والصبر: حبس النفس عما تنازع إليه.

JISHUMI:v2p988#2/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p988#2/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p988#2/r7.claim: Ṭālūt and the believers with him went out to fight Goliath and his troops.
JISHUMI:v2p988#2/r7.anchor: يعني طالوت والمؤمنين معه خرجوا إلى محاربة جالوت وجنوده

JISHUMI:v2p988#2/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p988#2/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p988#2/r8.claim: They asked God to enable them to endure patiently in jihad.

JISHUMI:v2p988#2/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p988#2/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p988#2/r9.claim: They asked God to make them steadfast so that they would not flee.
JISHUMI:v2p988#2/r9.anchor: أي وفقنا للثبوت حتى لا نفر

JISHUMI:v2p988#2/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p988#2/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p988#2/r10.claim: Their request for victory means asking for success in fighting the unbelievers.
JISHUMI:v2p988#2/r10.anchor: أي على جهادهم، ونصره تعالى يكون بوجهين

JISHUMI:v2p988#2/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p988#2/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p988#2/r11.claim: One form of divine victory strengthens believers' hearts, weakens unbelievers' hearts, instills terror, and causes discord that leads to failure.
JISHUMI:v2p988#2/r11.anchor: بالألطاف تقوي قلوب المؤمنين، ويوهن قلوب الكافرين، ورعب يدخل عليهم، واختلاف كلمة يؤدي إلى فشل.

JISHUMI:v2p988#2/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p988#2/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p988#2/r12.claim: The other form of victory is God's support through the angels, as at Badr.
JISHUMI:v2p988#2/r12.anchor: الثاني: بإمداد الملائكة كما فعله يوم بدر،

JISHUMI:v2p988#2/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p988#2/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p988#2/r13.claim: The unbelieving people are Goliath's people.

JISHUMI:v2p988#2/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p988#2/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p988#2/r14.claim: It is praiseworthy to ask God for help and the ability to persevere, relying wholly on Him.
JISHUMI:v2p988#2/r14.anchor: الآية تدل على حسن سؤال المعونة من الله تعالى، والتوفيق على المصابرة والانقطاع إليه تعالى،

JISHUMI:v2p988#2/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p988#2/r15.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p988#2/r15.claim: Believers must follow this example, relying on God in all affairs; recounting earlier communities teaches this practice.
JISHUMI:v2p988#2/r15.anchor: وتدل على أن الواجب علينا أن نقتدي بهم في ذلك، فنتكل على الله في جميع أمورنا،

BURHAN:v1p393/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p393/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p393/r1.claim: The alif is omitted from “when they came out against Goliath” because the episode is viewed as spiritual and elevated; the alif is kept in the account of David killing the embodied Goliath.
BURHAN:v1p393/r1.anchor: حذف لأنه الاسم ﴿ وقتل داود جالوت ﴾ ثبت لأنه مجسد محسوس

BURHAN:v1p393/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p393/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p393/r2.claim: The alif in “its gates were opened” is omitted because the opened gates are spiritual and elevated; it is retained in “the gates are opened for them” and in the count of seven gates as concrete worldly forms.
BURHAN:v1p393/r2.anchor: ﴿ وفتحت أبوابها ﴾ محذوف لأنها من حيث فتحت ملكوتية علوية

BURHAN:v1p393/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p393/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p393/r3.claim: Alif is retained in locusts as a tangible single specimen but omitted in frogs, whose plural is treated as a spiritual sign rather than a single tangible instance.
BURHAN:v1p393/r3.anchor: وكذلك الجراد والضفدع الأول ثابت فهو الذى فى الواحدة المحسوسة والثانى محذوف لأنه ليس فى الواحدة المحسوسة

BURHAN:v1p393/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p393/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p393/r4.claim: The spelling of amthal changes with specificity: alif is omitted for unspecified universal likenesses and retained when the comparison is specified, such as pearl whiteness and purity; detailed tangible examples differ from implicit ones.
BURHAN:v1p393/r4.anchor: حذفت لأنها أمثال كلية لم يتعين فيها للفهم جهة التماثل

BURHAN:v1p393/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p393/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p393/r5.claim: Repeated forms for the trumpet blast and the earth's crushing differ because the first is spiritual and known through faith, while the second is physical and imaginable.
BURHAN:v1p393/r5.anchor: الأولى محذوفة لأنها روحانية لا تعلم إلا إيمانا والثانية ثابتة جسمانية

BURHAN:v1p393/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p393/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p393/r6.claim: The alif in “my book” is omitted as spiritual, while that in “my account” is retained as worldly, although both refer to the afterlife.
BURHAN:v1p393/r6.anchor: محذوفة لأنه ملكوتى وألف ﴿ حسابيه ﴾ ثابتة لأنها ملكية

BURHAN:v1p393/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p393/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p393/r7.claim: The spiritual case is written without alif, while the tangible worldly possession retains it.
BURHAN:v1p393/r7.anchor: ملكوتية / وماليه / ملكى محسوس فحذف الأول وثبت الثانى

BURHAN:v1p393/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p393/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p393/r8.claim: For subhan, alif is omitted as spiritual except in one disputed place; the author prefers omission there too, since the Prophet's elevated presence is not distracted by worldly movement.
BURHAN:v1p393/r8.anchor: ومن أسقط فلعلو حال المصطفى صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يشغله عن الحضور تقلبه فى الملكوت الخطاب فى الملك وهو أولى الوجهين

DAMGHANI:v1p353/r17.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p353/r17.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p353/r17.claim: Afrigh means pour out; the examples ask for patience to be poured and molten metal to be poured over a wall.
